_meta.what: Catalyst radar — the 'born-big' overnight-unicorn watchlist (methodology #5, the highest-priority signal class). Spin-offs, mergers, acquisitions, carve-outs and take-privates that mint a $1B+ entity overnight: a fresh balance sheet, a brand-identity reckoning, NO existing sponsorships, and budget authority being set right now. This is the detection inbox; promising events get promoted into data/prospects.json as scored prospects.
_meta.why: These companies are the rare combination the mandate prizes most. They are easy to miss because they did not exist (in their current form) yesterday, so we scan for them every run and log them here BEFORE they are fully scored — so none slips through.
_meta.schema: events[]: id, name, type (spinoff|merger|acquisition|carveout|take_private), counterparty (parent/acquirer/target), event_date (ISO; announced or close), status (announced|imminent|closed), new_valuation, sector, series_hint (F1|FE|either), why_it_matters, confidence (VERIFIED|REPORTED|ESTIMATE), source, promoted_to (prospect id, or null if still on the radar), triage (next action).
_meta.freshness: engine/scoring.py treats a catalyst as FRESH (a ranking boost) while status is announced/imminent OR the event is within CATALYST_FRESH_DAYS (~18 months). View the radar: python3 engine/catalysts.py

events.name: Versigent (Aptiv EDS spin-off)
events.sector: EV electrical distribution systems ('the nervous system of the electric vehicle')
events.why_it_matters: Aptiv spun out its Electrical Distribution Systems business into a standalone public company (ticker VGNT), distributed to shareholders 1 Apr 2026 (1 VGNT per 3 APTV). Forecast ~$9.1-9.4B 2026 revenue, ~$300M post-deal cash. A multi-billion EV-electrical pure-play born overnight with an EV-momentum story is a natural Formula E brand-reckoning candidate. CAVEAT: it is an auto component supplier, not a SaaS buyer - triage whether it is a sponsor profile (brand/talent halo) or merely an industry supplier before promoting.
events.triage: Verify it would actually sponsor (vs. just supply). If yes, score for Formula E and check already_present via Aptiv's existing motorsport ties.

events.name: Also (Rivian micromobility spin-out)
events.counterparty: Rivian (parent; RJ Scaringe on board) + Eclipse / Greenoaks
events.sector: Micromobility — electric bikes + small/quad EVs (TM-B e-bike at $4,500; TM-Q quads; autonomous delivery for DoorDash)
events.why_it_matters: A textbook born-big catalyst — a Rivian skunkworks spun out and hit $1B in ~a year. BUT triaged NOT eligible as a 1440 sponsorship prospect: it is a CONSUMER / hardware micromobility brand (a vehicle maker), not the B2B enterprise-tech ICP the engine targets; an early-stage, capex-heavy startup whose capacity for a $3-5M/yr x 3yr deal is doubtful while it funds manufacturing + autonomy; and its motorsport logic would be consumer mass-marketing, not B2B credibility/hospitality. The FE tie is thematic (electric/sustainability) only.
events.triage: DO NOT PROMOTE — consumer-hardware profile, not the B2B ICP; capacity/stage questionable. WATCH only: reconsider if its commercial/fleet arm (TM-Q, DoorDash autonomy) matures into a B2B brand with a sustainability narrative and real sponsorship budget.

events.name: Cohesity (Veritas data-protection merger)
events.new_valuation: ~$1.5B pro-forma ARR; 2026 IPO benchmarked vs Rubrik (~$14.5B)
events.why_it_matters: The Veritas combination created a ~$1.5B-ARR category leader overnight, now steering to a 2026 IPO - the exact born-big profile. Already worked as the F1 proof brief (Cohesity -> Cadillac, 82/100).
events.triage: Promoted + shipped. Example of a merger catalyst converted to a hero.

events.name: Quantinuum (Honeywell spin-off)
events.new_valuation: ~$12.7B IPO target (27% above the $10B Sep-2025 round)
events.why_it_matters: A born-big Honeywell spin-off heading into a ~$12.7B IPO with a freshly expanded C-suite - never entered motorsport. Already a scored prospect (Quantinuum -> Aston Martin, 76/100).
events.triage: Promoted. Example of a spin-off catalyst already in the pipeline.

events.name: DXC Technology (CSC + HPE Enterprise Services merger/spin-off)
events.counterparty: Computer Sciences Corp + HPE Enterprise Services (Reverse Morris Trust: HPE spin-off merged into CSC)
events.why_it_matters: PROOF THE PATTERN CONVERTS. A ~$26B end-to-end IT-services company born overnight from a 2017 merger/spin-off - which went on to become a Scuderia Ferrari Team Partner (multi-year, from the Miami GP, May 2023; logo on the SF-23, race suits and helmets). The clearest evidence that a born-big B2B-tech company is exactly the profile that signs an F1 sponsorship. Reference/proof example.
events.triage: DO NOT TARGET - already_present on the F1 grid (Ferrari partner). Kept as the proof-of-conversion case study, not a live prospect.
